query: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists during exposure above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than developing unstable surface oxides that crack or spall? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted differences, the applicable exposure and material-state boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsifying observation.

generation.hypothesis: The formation and persistence of a stable, coherent protective oxide layer on CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) during exposure above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres is governed by the preferential segregation of Cr to the surface and its ability to form a continuous Cr2O3 layer. The presence of Al as X enhances this behavior by promoting the formation of a mixed Al2O3-Cr2O3 oxide layer, which is more thermodynamically stable and resistant to cracking or spalling compared to oxides formed in alloys with Si or Mn as X.
generation.material_initial_state: CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
generation.intervention: Substitute X in CrFeCoNiX with Al, Si, or Mn and expose the alloys to an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere at temperatures above 900 °C.
generation.conditions: Oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, temperature > 900 °C, exposure time sufficient to allow oxide layer formation (e.g., 100 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: Preferential segregation of Cr to the surface and the formation of a continuous Cr2O3 or mixed Al2O3-Cr2O3 layer.
generation.mechanism: Cr segregation to the surface enables the formation of a protective Cr2O3 oxide layer. When Al is present as X, it further enhances the stability of the oxide layer by forming a mixed Al2O3-Cr2O3 layer, which has higher thermodynamic stability and better mechanical integrity compared to oxides formed with Si or Mn as X. In contrast, Si or Mn may form less protective or more brittle oxides, leading to cracking or spalling under thermal stress.
generation.predicted_outcome: CrFeCoNiAl will form a stable, coherent oxide layer with minimal cracking or spalling, while CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn will form less stable oxide layers that are prone to cracking or spalling.
generation.baseline: CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn alloys, which are expected to form less stable oxide layers compared to CrFeCoNiAl.
generation.boundary: Applicable to CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states exposed to oxidative or corrosive atmospheres at temperatures above 900 °C.
generation.uncertainty: The exact contribution of Si and Mn to the stability and mechanical integrity of the oxide layer is not well understood, and the role of multiphase microstructures in oxide formation and stability is unclear.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Al, Si, or Mn in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state. Expose the alloys to an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere at 1000 °C for 100 hours. Characterize the oxide layers using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to assess composition, morphology, and mechanical integrity.
measurements: Adhesion strength of oxide layer (scratch test or similar)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If CrFeCoNiAl does not form a more stable and coherent oxide layer compared to CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn, or if the oxide layers on CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn exhibit comparable or superior stability and mechanical integrity to CrFeCoNiAl, the hypothesis is falsified.
